analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 808-823): it adds a paragraph describing segmented paged KV admission with parked 64 MiB segments. Parked segments are retained per pool up to min(2 GiB, slot grant/8), outside the grant, floor and ledger charge. They use zero-fill-on-demand host pages, are dropped on refused admission, on process-wide release requests and after 30 s of engine idleness, and can be disabled via DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION=0 and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP=0. The supplied base units (lines 822-1621) contain no changed lines, so this is documentation only; no code, keys, auth or protocol changes were supplied.

Security-relevant observations, not findings, because the implementation (EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift, PagedKVGroup.swift, KVPoolReclaimer) is not in the supplied evidence:
1. Parked, reused segments are described as reinstalled for the next admission of the same size class. If a segment is not zeroed or overwritten before reuse, residual KV from a prior request could cross requests or tenants (T-028, A-001). The text says new segments are zero-filled but says nothing about zeroing reused parked ones. The next pass should check that reuse is fully overwritten or masked before it is read.
2. Parking occurs outside the memory ledger. This could affect admission headroom and availability (T-029). The text says it is bounded and dropped on pressure.
3. The TTFT-oriented changes might alter cache timing observations (T-041/SEC-035). This is a latency optimization with no cache-scope, TTL, HMAC or at-rest change, so the SSD cache posture is unchanged.

No regression is established from the documentation alone. The segment reuse and zeroing contract remains unverified because the code is not supplied.
